title: token-throttle-ripples-notebook
content:
Notes to self: investigating recurring 401/429 pattern that appears to ripple across a few customers around midnight UTC. This is a scratchpad — rough chronology, commands I ran, hypotheses, and quick repros.

High-level summary:
- Symptoms: Intermittent 401 (Unauthorized) for valid API keys (short bursts, ~30s-2m), followed by a cluster of 429s for the same client over the next 5–15 minutes.
- Affected surface: Hosted API + some Dedicated customers routing through the same edge region.
- Correlation: spikes often align with scheduled key-rotation jobs (customer side) and our midnight autoscaler bursts.

Observed error snippets (copied from curl responses):
- 401 response body: {"error":"unauthorized","message":"Invalid authentication credentials"}
- 429 response body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"Rate window exceeded","retry_after":15}
- Response headers seen during incidents: Retry-After: 15, X-RateLimit-Limit: 600, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: 1700

Timestamps / timeline (local notes):
- 2025-11-02T23:58:10Z customer A reported 401 on one replica of their service
- 2025-11-02T23:58:20Z internal logs show ephemeral-key-refresh for customer A (rotation request to KMS)
- 2025-11-02T23:58:45Z same client started receiving 429s; other clients on same node unaffected for first 30s
- 2025-11-03T00:03:12Z traffic redistributed by smart-routing fallback -> several requests routed to cheaper model variant; 429s subsided gradually by 00:15

Commands and quick repros I executed (local workstation):
1) Basic auth check (works outside incident):
   curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
   -> 200 OK (text/stream)

2) Repro script I used to hammer one key (simulate client):
   for i in {1..120}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate; sleep 0.2; done
   Observed pattern: 200 for ~80 reqs, then burst of 401s (3-8), then 429s for ~90s, then resume 200s.

3) Header introspection to capture rate headers:
   curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate | sed -n '1,20p'
   -> confirmed X-RateLimit-* headers present during 429 windows

4) Force rotate key via simulated KMS microflow and retry immediately:
   # rotate (test-only) -> server returns rotated token
   curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/internal/rotate-key?cust=A
   Then repeated above repro loop using new token -> immediate 401 for a few requests, then 200/429 pattern as above.

Logs worth copying into ticket:
- edge-proxy: ERROR auth: token-validate failed: signature-mismatch (vault-kms-attempt=2) at 2025-11-02T23:58:45Z
- token-service: INFO rotate-request received for cust=A (requestor=svc-deploy) 2025-11-02T23:58:20Z
- rate-limiter: WARN window-exhausted client=custA node=us-east-1a bucket=10m

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Race between client-side key rotation and our edge cache of token->customer mapping. If client rotates and starts sending new key before caches/propagation complete, first requests from new key get 401. Retries from client then flood same rate bucket (old+new key mapping collapse) causing 429.
2) KMS latency/backoff causes token-service to report transient validation failures (signature-mismatch) for rotated keys; proxy treats as auth failure (401) rather than retryable validation error.
3) Smart routing fallback/flood to cheaper model causes per-route throttles to be hit after auth churn; effectively two-phase failure (auth -> then rate carrying over to model route).
4) Client SDK behavior: simultaneous retry of many in-flight requests during rotation causing thundering herd against same quota bucket.

Quick checks to validate hypotheses:
- Reproduce with two distinct keys for same customer issued close together: try sending alternating requests with keyA and keyB and observe if buckets unify (I did a limited run; saw Remaining count drop faster than expected).
- Introduce artificial sleep after rotate to simulate propagation delay: delayed sends avoided 401/429 cascade.

Temporary mitigations applied during incidents:
- Whitelisted customer A IP on edge for 30min to allow graceful drain (reduced 429 noise)
- Increased per-customer burst window in rate-limiter for the affected project (10% bump) — emergency only
- Began feature flag rollout to make auth failures that look like signature-mismatch return 409 with guidance instead of 401 (so SDKs can refresh without hitting quota)

Repro checklist for staging (what to run next):
- Script that: rotate key via internal API -> immediately run high-concurrency requests (100 qps) with new key -> capture exact sequence codes + X-RateLimit headers
- Run same flow with 2s / 5s / 10s delays to measure threshold where ripple disappears
- Repeat with two separate app instances starting simultaneous requests (to simulate SDKs with in-flight retries)

Instrumentation gaps / logging asks (for follow-up tickets):
- Edge should emit token-hash + orbit-id mapping snapshots at time of validation (not raw token), to cross-reference quickly
- Rate-limiter needs per-original-key line items (not just customer aggregation) for 2m rollups during incidents
- Token-service should log KMS latencies and return codes where signature verification failed

Open questions / TODOs:
- What exact cache TTLs exist on edge for token->customer mapping? (I think 15s default, but need confirmation)
- Do SDKs auto-retry on 401? If so with what backoff and jitter? (dangerous if many clients do so simultaneously)
- Can we make auth failures that are likely transient return a non-quota-impacting code temporarily (409?) so client retries don't hit rate windows?

Links and artifacts:
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RINF-3421 (investigate auth->rate ripple)
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01M0KQ8/thread/pyy-401-429-ripple (internal log snippets)
- PR that touched token-cache logic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/555

Immediate next steps for me:
- Build the full repro script for staging and add to this doc (goal: reproduce end-to-end without touching production)
- Ask infra for edge cache TTLs and current rollout of token-cache change (ping @infra)
- Draft mini-runbook for on-call to apply quick mitigations (whitelist, burst bump, feature-flag auth response) and link it in the Jira ticket

Notes / random thoughts:
- The two-phase failure feels like an impedance mismatch: auth layer says "not my problem" (401) but rate layer inherits the failure when retries occur. Better inter-layer signaling could avoid double punishment.
- If we can detect "recently rotated" keys and mark first N requests from new token as soft-validated (while background verification finalizes), that might eliminate the spike.

Personal to-dos (short):
- [ ] finalize repro script (staging)
- [ ] add more precise timeline from logs (edge + token-service)
- [ ] sync with SDK owners about retry behavior

End of scratchpad. Keep this file as a private user note until we have a reproducible test and then copy into shared_drives/engineering/observability/incidents/ with a cleaned runbook.
